findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There were tortillas observed to be stored directly in a grocery bag on the cook-line. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the tortillas were switched into a food-grade container. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be properly sanitized. Ensure that food is stored in a package that protects the integrity of the contents and does not expose it to contaminants.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was observed to be raw chicken in a cooler drawer above raw pork. There was also raw bacon stored behind eggrolls in another cooler drawer. CORRECTED- The raw pork was moved to be above the raw chicken and the raw bacon was moved in front of the eggrolls. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display. A storage order handout was provided to the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(A) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (A) Hot water manual operations by immersion for at least 30 seconds and as specified under § 4-501.111.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The following TCS foods were observed to be held above 41F: 

- The Traditional Barbecue sauce that states to “Refrigerate After Opening” on the label was observed to be stored outside of cold holding under the steam table. The PIC stated that it was opened two days ago and voluntarily discarded it. This barbecue sauce was previously placed under time as control, but the facility has since ceased using that method. The PIC stated that the sauce will be stored in the cooler moving forward. 
- There were portioned cups of sauces that were observed to be stored outside of cold holding. These sauces were placed outside of cold holding at 10am, according to the PIC, and it was discussed to discard these by 2pm. The PIC stated that they will cold hold these sauces on ice going forward. 
- The preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F in the bottom of the cooler and lettuce probed to be at 48F in the top of the cooler. The PIC stated that the lid of the preparation cooler was left open overnight, but that only limes were left in the cooler. The TCS foods in the top of the cooler were placed under Time as Control to allow them to still work out of the cooler. The PIC stated that these foods were placed in the cooler at 10:30am and will be discarded by 2:30pm. The foods in the bottom of the cooler were recently placed in it and were moved into the walk-in cooler. The bottom of the preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 38F by the end of the inspection. It was discussed to make sure to check the temperature of the cooler before placing TCS foods in it if it has been left open overnight. It is also recommended to close the lid of the preparation cooler in-between uses. The temperature of the preparation cooler will be spot checked at the 7/14/2026 follow up for violation #48. 

Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple TCS food items made in-house in the walk-in cooler that were observed to not be date-marked, including:

- A container of rice. 
- A container of beans. 
- A container of cheese sauce. 

The kitchen manager date-marked these items during the inspection. There was also inconsistent date-marking observed in the walk-in cooler. According to the PIC, staff members were date-marking use the day of the month and the year (ex: 3/26). Ensure that the method of date-marking is consistent and that staff are trained to date-mark TCS food items that are made or opened in-house and are held for over 24 hours. Date-marking will be spot checked at the 7/14/2026 scheduled follow-up for violation #48.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to use a wiping cloth to wipe food-contact surfaces and store it on the counter in between uses. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are trained to store wiping cloths in the sanitizer bucket in-between uses to prevent bacteria growth on the wiping cloth.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were no food handler certificates available for any of the employees. The PIC was instructed to ensure that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The Certified Food Protection Manager was observed to not have their Allergen training certificate. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility that has their Allergen training during all hours of operation and food preparation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

[PF]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: REPEAT - The front counter sanitizer bucket was observed to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium and the sanitizer bucket by the cook-line was observed to be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED - Both sanitizer buckets were re-made and tested to be at 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are routinely checked to make sure they are at the label-recommended concentration. Sanitizer buckets should typically be changed every two to four hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed many of the foods in the walk-in cooler to be above 41F. Foods probed include: Carnitas (50F), Cheese Sauce (50F), Consommé (51F), Raw Beef (51F), Raw Hamburger (50F), Cheese Sauce x2 (52F), Bacon (51F), Refried Beans (51F), Milk (51F), Raw Beef (52F), Cheese Sauce x3 (54F), Sour Cream (48F), Cut Lettuce (53F), Egg Rolls (53F). All out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are kept at 41F or below. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate cold-holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the drawer coolers under the griddle to not be holding temperatures below 41F. Items in coolers are as follows: Raw Chicken (53.5F), Raw Beef (52F), Raw Marinated Chicken (51.5F), and shredded cheese (55F). All items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are kept at or below 41F. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate reevaluate cooler temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 TCS items being stored out of refrigeration. The items were: Barbecue Sauce (Ambient temperature), mayonnaise (75F), feta (54F). All were voluntarily thrown away. The barbecue sauce was open on a shelf at room temp, and had been there for a while. Facility was attempting to store the mayo and feta in an ice bath. When preparing an ice bath, ensure that food containers are submerged to the top of the container in ice. Ice must then be replenished as needed to keep foods at or below 41F. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate the cold holding of these items.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the walk-in cooler at the facility to be failing. Multiple foods inside the cooler probed at above 41F. See violation 22  regarding the walk-in cooler for more information. Ensure cooler is repaired or replaced. Inspector will return 07/31/2025 to reevaluate the cooler’s ability to hold temperatures at 41F or below.

Inspector observed the drawer coolers at the facility to be failing. Multiple foods inside the cooler probed at above 41F. See violation 22 regarding drawer coolers for more information. Ensure cooler is repaired or replaced. Inspector will return 07/31/2025 to reevaluate the cooler’s ability to hold temperatures at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a spatula being used to scoop carnitas in the walk-in cooler to be stored improperly. The spatula was sitting on the shelving in the cooler next to the carnitas. Ensure that while utensils are in use they are stored in the food being served with the handle sticking up. Alternatively, utensils may also be stored on a clean and sanitized work surface while not in use.

3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 2 utensils in need of repair or replacement in the kitchen. The first utensil in need of replacement or repair was the juicer. The paint on the juicer is flaking from the surface. The second utensil is the fine mesh strainer hanging in front of the ice machine. Loose wires are sticking off the side of the strainer basket. Ensure these items are repaired or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(A) Good Repair and Calibration. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several instances of a #55 violation at the establishment.

1) The floor of the kitchen was covered in water and food debris upon the inspector’s arrival. Ensure that the floor is kept free of large amounts of water and food debris.

2) The cold-water outlets in the floor behind the sink have been sealed into the floor with a material that is not smooth and easily cleanable. The material was observed to hold food debris and soils. Ensure this material is either smoothed or replaced to make it easily cleanable.

3) The walk-in cooler compressor is leaking water on the floor of the walk-in cooler and possibly foods inside. Ensure this is repaired to prevent the contamination of other surfaces and items in the cooler.

Ensure these areas are maintained and kept in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink soap dispenser was out-of-order upon arrival. PIC explained that employees had been washing hands at the triple sink using mounted soap located there. Inspector advised that facility still uses hand-sink to wash hands, and to continue using soap from the triple sink, as they are located just opposite one another in the kitchen. PIC stated that a call to repair the soap dispenser has already been made, and that it should be fixed by tomorrow morning. Ensure that hand sinks are properly supplied to allow for hand washing procedures. Inspector will return 03/20/2025 to re-asses soap dispenser.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw eggs being stored over beef in the facility’s walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved them so that they were above raw chicken instead. Ensure that raw meats are stored in proper order (fish, beef and pork, eggs, and poultry; top to bottom).
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
The facility has a number of flies present in back area of the kitchen. Flies are observed in-contact with hanging equipment, ice machine, containers of flour and onions, and other various equipment in the kitchen. See that pests are eliminated.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11:  Observed the facility to have a number of priority violations related to foods and practices not being monitored. The facility has been warned that the walk-in cooler has a history of failure (noted during the last routine inspection in July as well). The cooler is not being monitored. There is a pest control issue in the back room and the ice machine baffle is molded. There are significant concerns that could have been addressed if the facility had an active monitoring system. 


Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink is positioned in such a way that it cannot have anything other than the steam table in the alleyway. Upon entry, a tall bucket was observed at brim level of the sink. As the steam table is position in a manner that blocks half of the entry points to the sink, see that the walkway to the hand sink remains unobstructed. The bucket was moved during the inspection. If the hand sink is obstructed hands may not be properly washed and food borne illness has a potential to spread.   

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-101.11:  There are observed molded strawberries in the walk-in cooler. Discarded during the inspection. 
FOOD shall be in safe condition.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The facility has a number of fruit flies present which are in contact with onions, flour, ice and all uncovered foods within the facility. See that pest control is provided to eliminate the pests. The presence of flies indicates that cleaning may not be sufficient. (See violation #16) The facility should conduct a detail cleaning to support elimination of the pests, properly cover containers of food so pests cannot enter, and keep equipment covered so flies do not contact the surfaces. Eliminate the flies. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.comment:
6-403.11: There is observed a number of personal items throughout the kitchen. There are sweatshirts in the facility hanging on can racks and  phone on the steam table. There should be a designated area for employee items. 

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.comment: No hand washing station is available at this location during this event. Education was conducted and the stand was able to use a neighboring location to continue operations today. Ensure that hand washing is available at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.
